title: Read Analog Voltage
description: Turn a potentiometer knob and watch the Arduino measure the voltage on pin A0, from 0 to 5 volts, in the Serial Monitor.

steps.clip: Let's gather our parts: an Arduino Uno, a breadboard, a 10k potentiometer, three jumper wires and a USB cable.
Push the potentiometer into the top half of the breadboard, so each of its three legs sits in its own column.
hints: Three neighbouring columns, all in rows a to e, work well.
Make sure no two legs share the same column.

steps.clip: Take a black wire and connect one outer leg of the potentiometer to a GND pin on the Arduino.
hints: Put the wire in a free hole in the same column as an outer leg.
Any GND pin on the Arduino works.

steps.clip: Now take a red wire and connect the other outer leg to the 5V pin on the Arduino.
hints: Use the outer leg you haven't wired yet.
The 5V pin is on the power header, next to the GND pins.

steps.clip: Finally, use a green wire to connect the middle leg of the potentiometer to pin A0.
hints: The middle leg is the wiper; its voltage changes as you turn the knob.
Pin A0 is on the analog header, near the power pins.

steps.clip: Upload the sketch, open the Serial Monitor at 9600 baud, and turn the knob. You'll see the voltage go from 0 up to 5 volts.
